commits.author: Giulio Ardoino
commits.subject: fix: contain a long session title without truncating it
commits.body:
#67 stopped a long title from overflowing the mobile layout, and the
min-width: 0 it added is what actually does that: a grid child cannot
shrink below its content without it. The `white-space: nowrap` alongside
it went further than the overflow needed, though — it collapses every
multi-line card title to a single ellipsised line. The cards have always
wrapped, and the README screenshots show two-line titles, so the app
stopped matching its own documentation.

Breaking the word contains it just as well while keeping the wrapping,
and covers the case plain wrapping cannot: a title that is one unbroken
token. Measured against the real stylesheet at a 390px viewport, with a
long spaced title and a 128-character unbroken one: nowrap gave 1
truncated line each, break-word gives 4 wrapped lines each, neither
overflowing the card or the viewport.

The desktop sidebar keeps its single-line ellipsis: a compact row is the
point there, its own rule already sets it, and the full title is in the
tooltip.

The regression guard now asserts the invariant — a long title must break
rather than widen its card — rather than the nowrap/ellipsis spelling,
which pinned the truncation itself. Its selectors are anchored and scoped
to one rule block, because a bare `.session-card h3` also matches the
tail of `.sidebar-sessions .session-card h3` and read the sidebar's
deliberate nowrap as the mobile regression.

+   case plain wrapping cannot: a title that is a single unbroken token.

commits.body:
- Show the "Other" free-text field by default in question prompts
  unless the tool explicitly disables it with custom: false, since
  the question tool omits the field when relying on its default.
- Selecting a preset option now clears any typed custom text (and
  vice versa) for single-choice questions, avoiding accidental
  combined answers like "Black, Test".
- Highlight the previously chosen option(s), including a typed
  custom answer, when viewing a past question in the history modal.

commits.subject: feat: publish the web app to GitHub Pages, base-path-aware PWA
commits.body:
- Add a workflow that builds web/ with vite's --base set to the
  repo name (GitHub Pages serves project sites from /<repo>/) and
  deploys it via actions/deploy-pages.
- Make the PWA assets work under any base path: index.html and the
  manifest now use relative URLs, and the service worker derives
  its app-shell and cache URLs from self.registration.scope instead
  of hardcoded root paths. Registration in main.tsx now passes
  import.meta.env.BASE_URL as the sw.js path and scope.

+## Progressive Web App (PWA)
+
+The web app is installable and is published straight from this repo via GitHub Pages, at
+https://giuliastro.github.io/harness-remote/. Open that URL over HTTPS and browsers will offer to
+add it to the home screen / app list, opening in its own standalone window.
+
+- A service worker caches the app shell (`index.html`, the manifest, and the icons) plus other
+  same-origin static assets on a stale-while-revalidate basis, so the UI still loads offline or on
+  a flaky connection after the first visit.
+- Requests to your opencode/bridge server are never cached — they go to whatever host you
+  configured in Settings, cross-origin from wherever the PWA itself is hosted, so session data
+  always comes from the live server.
+- The service worker is skipped entirely in the native Android app (Capacitor) and in local dev
+  builds; it only registers in production web builds.
+
+Because the app talks to your server cross-origin, the server needs the PWA's origin listed
+in `--cors`:
+
+```bash
+npx -y opencode-ai serve --hostname 0.0.0.0 --port 4096 --cors https://giuliastro.github.io
+```
+
 ## Technology Stack
 
 - frontend: React + TypeScript + Vite
